assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visionary, densely patterned prose, with memory and the body built into a large metaphysical project (Blinding, Solenoid). The voice is highly distinctive, and the formal ambition and imaginative depth are sustained across volumes. The oeuvre also includes poetry, which suggests linguistic command beyond the novels.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would cover an expansive, inward and cosmological prose imagination rooted in Romanian, joining poetic and novelistic registers.
assessment.maturity: A long, cumulative body of work in which later books extend the earlier ones. The central achievement appears settled and durable.
uncertainties: The assessment relies on public knowledge and on translations, which may flatter or flatten the density of the Romanian prose.
Coverage of the poetry and early work is thinner than coverage of the major novels.
Some of the sprawling architecture may be uneven; this is hard to judge without full-corpus reading.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Remade Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and sustained dialogue with inherited forms (Songs of Mihyar the Damascene; A Time Between Ashes and Roses). Formal and linguistic achievement is the core claim, and its significance for modern Arabic poetry is widely discussed.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would cover poetic renewal of Arabic, with essays on tradition and modernity as secondary context.
assessment.maturity: An oeuvre of many decades with a long reception history. Poetic and critical influence is well established.
uncertainties: Poetry in translation loses much of the prosodic and intertextual achievement, so the central claim is difficult to verify outside Arabic.
The essays and the poetry may call for different weighting in a citation.
Public controversy around the writer's statements should not be treated as literary evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hybrid works remake the boundaries between classical scholarship, lyric, narrative and visual form (Autobiography of Red; Nox). The voice and formal inventiveness are unusual, and the intellectual depth comes from sustained engagement with antiquity and with grief.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would concern formal invention across poetry, essay, translation-adjacent work and drama, rather than a single genre.
assessment.maturity: A substantial body of work with recurring concerns. It is unclear whether the later work deepens or merely varies the strongest books.
uncertainties: Genre-crossing makes it hard to define the scope of a citation.
Several of the best-known works are book-objects or formally unusual editions, so format may affect how they are read.
Weight across the whole oeuvre, beyond a few celebrated books, is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large poetic sequences and landscape-scale interventions turn suffering into collective memorial form (Purgatory; Anteparadise). The ambition is distinctive and the work is closely tied to historical trauma. The central question is how far the poetry on the page holds up apart from the public gestures.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would address poetry that fuses language, place and memory in Spanish.
assessment.maturity: A decades-long project with consistent preoccupations. Its durability probably depends on how well the page-based work survives its historical moment.
uncertainties: Landscape and visual interventions are partly non-textual, so their weight as literature is contestable.
Translation risk is high for sustained poetic sequences.
Political and historical significance must not substitute for literary assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bilingual writing in Japanese and German turns linguistic estrangement into inventive narrative and poetic forms (The Emissary; Memoirs of a Polar Bear). The play with language is a real formal contribution. The voice is distinctive and the imaginative range is wide.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would turn on writing between two languages, with poetry, essays and drama as additional strands.
assessment.maturity: A substantial and still developing oeuvre. It is uncertain whether the strongest long-form works yet match the originality of the language experiments.
uncertainties: Much of the achievement depends on the interplay of two languages, which English translation cannot fully represent.
Corpus coverage is split across Japanese and German texts.
The depth of the later work relative to the earlier work is hard to gauge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A radically inward fiction builds a distinctive system of landscape, memory and mental images (The Plains; Border Districts). The voice is unmistakable and rigorously consistent. Formal austerity and intellectual seriousness are strengths.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would concern fiction as an investigation of consciousness, memory and the grammar of imagined places.
assessment.maturity: A cohesive late-career body of work. Because the project is so self-contained, its range may be narrower than that of other candidates.
uncertainties: The narrow thematic range may limit significance across the whole body of work.
Reception has been relatively late and limited, so durability is harder to assess.
Further evidence would be needed on how the work reads across the full corpus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Encyclopedic fiction links systems of power, scientific knowledge and countercultural imagination (Gravity's Rainbow; Mason & Dixon). The stylistic range and intellectual density are exceptional. The influence on later fiction is considerable, but reputation and mystique should not stand in for merit.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would address encyclopedic narrative forms and the novel's capacity to absorb scientific and political systems.
assessment.maturity: A long career, with the main achievement already clear. Whether later novels sustain the early peak is a matter of critical disagreement.
uncertainties: Quality across the whole oeuvre is uneven in critical opinion.
Density and allusiveness make translation difficult.
Significance may rest heavily on a few central works.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dreamlike narrative worlds destabilize ordinary psychology, space and causal storytelling (Frontier; Love in the New Millennium). The voice is distinctive and the formal radicalism is sustained over decades. The imaginative boldness is clear; the philosophical depth is harder to assess from translation.
assessment.attribution: Single credited writer. A citation would concern avant-garde Chinese fiction that departs from realist conventions through dream logic and estrangement.
assessment.maturity: A long and productive career. The question is whether the range of effects deepens across the work or repeats a single mode.
uncertainties: Only part of the large Chinese-language output is available in translation, so corpus coverage is limited.
Translated prose may obscure stylistic differences between books.
The critical consensus on which works are central is less clear.
